text: Every update asks for a little attention. A receipt. A newsletter. The same urgent message, delivered again.
For independent makers managing contest deadlines, the hard part is knowing when something actually needs a decision.
Only When It Matters is a small, local-first prototype: keep the first decision, and make the retry quiet.
This demonstration uses fictional events. It does not read a live inbox or send notifications.
The public replay shows five deliveries and four unique events.
A newsletter passes quietly. A receipt is recorded. An organizer request and a fictional winner notice request attention.
When that winner notice arrives again, the result contains no interruption and no action.
The first saved decision remains unchanged. The separate working agent uses the Strands Agents SDK and a local Qwen model.
In the recorded run, the model selected triage, supplied the unchanged event, and received one concrete action.
A fresh request retried the same event and received a quiet result.
The metrics tool then confirmed one unique event and one escalation decision.
Application hooks enforce one valid tool call and return the checked result.
Extra calls or changed inputs are rejected before execution.
This is enforced code, not a promise in a prompt.
Tests also inject failures before and after saving,
then check what happens on retry. The public page is a static replay, not the live model.
Counts are policy decisions, not verified wins or measured time saved.
Sender verification, real notification delivery, and multi-process coordination remain outside this prototype.
The source and architecture are public under the MIT license.
The aim is simple: let routine work stay routine, and make the next real decision clear.
